subject: [COMPANY] <> Encord
text:
Hey [NAME], I lead GTM efforts for Physical AI at Encord. We work with a
number of drone and autonomous systems teams on the data infrastructure
side to manage, annotate, and curate multi-sensor and aerial video data
that feeds their models.

Many of the customers that we work with (Zipline, Skydio, etc) partnered
with us as the scale of complexity started to break initial tooling across
multi-camera sensor fusion, large-volume flight data, edge-case mining
across diverse environments. The teams we work with at that stage are
usually either hitting walls with in-house annotation infrastructure or
spending engineering cycles maintaining pipelines that need to be automated.

Would be keen to explore any friction points the Elroy team is dealing with
across the data lifecycle and where we can add the most leverage as you're
continuing to scale.

Would you be open to a quick intro chat in the next week or two?

subject: Dusty <> Encord
text:

I lead GTM efforts for Physical AI at Encord. We work with companies across
robotics, AVs, drones, and other forms of autonomous systems to help them

in-house annotation infrastructure or spending engineering cycles

Curious whether that's a friction point for you right now; specifically
around how you're handling annotation and data curation as the autonomy
stack scales.

Would you be open to a quick intro chat in the next week or two?

subject: How Dolby is enriching metadata at scale - is this relevant?
text:
Hi [NAME],

Came across your profile and your description of building AI that pulls
deep metadata out of raw video immediately stood out - that's almost
exactly what we're working on with Dolby.

We're helping them ingest large content libraries, apply taxonomy rubrics
at scale, and feed structured metadata into their downstream GenAI
pipelines.

The problem they were solving is fragmented tooling making it hard to get
consistent, reliable data out of raw content at speed.

Given you're building near zero-touch workflows and wiring multimodal
models into your media supply chain, I suspect the data quality and ground
truth side of that equation comes up as a bottleneck.

I've attached a one-pager to anchor an inital conversation around - is it
worth 20 mins next week to share what's working for Dolby and a few other
content teams?

subject: agent data quality
text:
Hi [NAME],

Virtuals Protocol's agent commerce model only works if the underlying multimodal data stays clean: prompts, transcripts, images, and any generated assets all need consistent review and traceability as you iterate.

Encord is the data layer teams use to curate and evaluate unstructured datasets so model changes are driven by the right slices of data, not guesswork. That usually means faster iteration and fewer regressions when new modalities or edge cases show up.

Can we set up 20 minutes this week?

subject: Automating the Annotation pipeline at [COMPANY] <> Encord
text:
Hi [NAME],

The teams we work with doing L4 autonomy, 100TB+ datasets, camera + LiDAR +
radar fusion, hit the same wall as maritime perception: getting labeled
edge-case data fast enough to keep the model iteration loop tight. The
annotation tooling is usually what slows them down, not the modelling. I
see you're leading perception/autonomy at [COMPANY] and would be keen to
understand some of the areas where you're looking for lift.

Zeitview doubled their data throughput and improved recall by 12% once
their aerial annotation pipeline stopped fragmenting across tools. For ASV
perception, we can support vessel tracking in adverse weather, night ISR,
dense traffic. Encord handles video, LiDAR, and point cloud annotation
natively, with SAM3 pre-labelling and embedding search to pull the specific
failure scenarios out of raw mission data.

Would love to briefly connect on a quick call to get a better sense of your
current challenges.
